msalazar: Escalation from ACME SRE — after we consolidated tool names (removed tenant-prefix on a few handles) their production fleet started getting 400 schema errors on tool calls. They say nothing in their client changed.

samir_eng: Can you paste the failing request + the error body from our gateway? also which tenant/region?

msalazar: tenant=acme, region=us-west-2. Here's the curl they used (redacted API key):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{\n    "tool": "ACME/Translate",\n    "args": { "text": "hello" }\n  }'\n```

Response they got: 

```json
{
  "error": "schema_validation_error",
  "detail": "missing required field 'input' for tool translate (expected schema v2)",
  "status": 400
}
```

msalazar: We checked on the customer side — client indeed sends `text`. Historically the old handle accepted `text`. The new canonical tool expects `input`. So either they hit the old handler or a different tool entirely.

samir_eng: Oof. Do we have gateway logs showing which tool UUID the request routed to? that will confirm whether it resolved to the new canonical translate or an older tenant-scoped variant.

msalazar: Pasted gateway snippet from their request trace (timestamps scrubbed):

```
INFO resolve: incoming tool handle 'ACME/Translate' -> resolved_alias='acme_translate' -> resolved_tool_uuid=tool_9a3f (schema=input:v2)
INFO invoke: selected worker pool dedicated-usw2-translate -> picked instance gpu-04
INFO response: tool invocation failed schema_mismatch -> expected 'input', got 'text'\n```

samir_eng: That log line says resolved_tool_uuid=tool_9a3f which is the new v2 model. If customer previously used a different tool that accepted `text`, they'd have been routed to tool_3b2d maybe. So why is the client suddenly sending the old arg name against the new tool? Two hypotheses: 1) clients were pinned to an older alias that we recently pruned and they fell back to a tenant-prefixed alias that maps differently; or 2) our alias normalization is lowercasing/stripping slashes in an unexpected way and hitting an internal tenant shadow.

tyler_ops: quick check — registry-sync cron ran ~10:05 UTC and deploy-bot applied alias migration at 10:08. However cache TTL on our edge resolver is 30m (config: `EDGE_ALIAS_CACHE_TTL=1800s`). If a client had an in-memory mapping or DNS pinned to an older edge, they might still route to an instance that has old aliases. Also note we still have a tombstone TTL for renames: `ALIAS_TOMBSTONE_TTL=7d` which can create ambiguous matches for a window.

deploy-bot: registry-sync job completed: aliases migrated 2024-06-13T10:08:22Z, migration id=mg-20240613-acme. No failures recorded.

samir_eng: For immediate repro + mitigation: ask the customer to call the /v1/toolcall with explicit tool UUID instead of name (this bypasses alias resolution) and confirm behavior. Also we can run an admin cache invalidation for that tenant: 

```bash
# run from infra admin host
POST /admin/cache/invalidate?tenant=acme&scope=alias
# OR
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.redwood.ai/v1/cache/invalidate -d '{"tenant":"acme","scope":"alias"}'
```

msalazar: Customer tried the UUID route and it worked (no schema error). They confirmed their fleet is older client code that still emits `text`. They asked why alias resolution would change without them updating.

samir_eng: That matches: their clients likely relied on the tenant-prefixed handle `acme_translate` which we removed when we consolidated. In a short window, alias resolution prefers tenant-specific alias over global alias if both exist (by design) — but if the tenant alias was tombstoned recently we could route to a different UUID that expects different args. We need to confirm whether a tombstone record existed and whether alias normalization (casefold + slash -> underscore) created a collision.

tyler_ops: I checked the alias index: before migration we had `acme_translate -> tool_3b2d` (old schema expects `text`); after migration `translate -> tool_9a3f` (expects `input`). The tombstone entry `acme_translate` was removed but due to case-folding `ACME/Translate` normalized to `acme_translate` and hit a cache entry that still pointed to tool_3b2d on some resolvers. Not all edge nodes refreshed at the same time — we have a rollout gap across 3 zones.

samir_eng: Root cause summary: alias rename + normalization + staggered cache invalidation led some requests to still resolve to the old tenant-scoped tool uuid (which accepted `text`) while others resolved to the new canonical tool (expects `input`). Mix of routes -> intermittent schema validation failures.

support_lead: Action items:
- samir_eng to run a forced alias cache purge for acme (done: started).
- tyler_ops to shorten EDGE_ALIAS_CACHE_TTL default and push a playbook to avoid 30m drift for future migrations.
- We need an RFC to prevent ambiguous normalization collisions (slashes -> underscores) during renames.

samir_eng: I've executed the admin invalidate for tenant=acme and rolled a rolling restart of edge-resolver in us-west-2. I also triggered a one-off backfill to fix any alias tombstones.

msalazar: Customer confirmed after ~2m that their fleet is now consistently getting the new schema error if they send `text` (expected) and UUID calls succeed. They've scheduled an upgrade of client lib to v1.3 (which uses `input`) tonight.

tyler_ops: Follow-up: I'll propose reducing EDGE_ALIAS_CACHE_TTL to 60s for migrations and adding a migration-step 'cache-warm' window + propagation check. Also adding a post-migration probe that queries all edge nodes for resolved tool_uuid for a few example handles.

support_lead: assigning owner samir_eng for customer RCA and cross-team follow-ups. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

msalazar: noted, will update ACME SRE with RCA and mitigation steps (UUID fallback + client upgrade timeline).

samir_eng: putting notes into the migration runbook and filing a bug for alias normalization collision handling.

(END)
